sonnet.problem: The statement bundles two claims. It restates that no one can be discharged in wartime, then adds a second claim that the wicked can walk away from wickedness whenever they like. Only the second claim is being tested.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: This True statement mirrors the previous card. Card 10's right answer already states the righteous half of verse 14, so the wicked half is an easy restatement of the same futility, not a new fact.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question. An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The text leaves open whose eyes do not see sleep: 'the task that one performs... though his eyes do not see sleep.' The card gives it to the Teacher himself, and the joke adds a time, three in the morning, that the text does not give.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: This re-asks the point of card 16. Card 16's right answer already says a man is unable to comprehend the work under the sun, and the False statement here just repeats it for the wise man. It also gives away the answer, since an easy follow-up must ask something new.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
